story_type: aircraft crash drop test with dummies
hook: NASA filled an air taxi with crash dummies, then dropped it.
narration: NASA strapped crash dummies into an air taxi, hung it from a steel tower, and let it fall.
This crash was planned, at NASA's Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia.
The body is full scale, modeled after an air taxi, with dummies belted into the seats.
Sensors record how hard the hit lands, so engineers learn which materials soak up the force before it reaches a passenger.
A camera inside caught the dummies jolting in their seats as the body hit.
It was NASA's second drop of this kind, after a similar test in late twenty twenty two.
outcome: The body landed in one piece, and NASA collected the data to help make air taxis safer.
title: Air taxi dropped with dummies inside
description:
On June 24, 2025, researchers at NASA's Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, dropped a full-scale aircraft body modeled after an air taxi from a steel gantry to study which materials best absorb crash forces.

facts.claim: Langley researchers dropped a full-scale air taxi body from a gantry
facts.source_quote: Researchers at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, dropped a full-scale aircraft body, modeled after an air taxi, from a tall steel structure, known as a gantry, at the center’s Landing and Impact Research Facility.

facts.claim: Second test after one in late 2022; studies materials that absorb impact forces
facts.source_quote: This and a previous test in late 2022 allow researchers to investigate aircraft materials that best absorb impact forces in a crash to protect the passengers and cargo inside.

facts.claim: Data will help manufacturers design safer air taxis
facts.source_quote: The data collected will enable manufacturers to design safer advanced air mobility aircraft.
